```python
import sys

def write_text_to_memory(text):
    with open("memory.txt", "w") as file:
        file.write(text)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: python write_text_to_memory.py <text>")
        sys.exit(1)

    text = sys.argv[1]
    write_text_to_memory(text)
```

This program uses the `with` statement to open the file and write the text to it. The `write_text_to_memory` function takes the text as input and returns the modified text. The `sys.argv` list contains the command-line arguments passed to the program.
